inputs.text: Canada’s tougher rules targeting Nigerians and others should not be sold as a “necessary reminder.” That language turns people seeking safety into a supposed public-order problem and obscures how immigration enforcement can reproduce racialized exclusion. Bill C-12 received royal assent on March 26, 2026, but enactment is not proof of fairness. Border management must not come at the cost of asylum seekers’ rights or make vulnerable people absorb the consequences of political narratives about disorder. A system earns public trust by protecting people, not merely tightening restrictions.

subtopics: Opposition to framing immigration enforcement as a public-order response
